text:
maria: quick check — I hit a flaky failure in prod where model responses look corrupted for a small % of requests. I want to enable a very short-lived request/response capture for those requests to debug prompt/kv issues. asking for security sign-off.

maria: current plan: capture full request/response to an encrypted S3 bucket with 1-hour TTL, bucket access restricted to eng-ml and security, and a manual approval step to turn capture on per-incident. we would run for max 60 minutes and then auto-delete.

leo: +1 to short TTL. can we instead capture masked prompts (tokens redacted) and store a separate hashed_user_id rather than raw identifiers?

jordan: fyi tagging security requirements: must not store raw bearer tokens, PII (emails, ssn), or full credit-card strings. hashed_user_id is fine as long as hashing is salted per-environment and salt is rotated.

sec-bot: Reminder: logging-redaction-policy v2.1 applies — see https://internal.redwood/sec-logging#ephemeral-capture for required controls and audit steps.

maria: thanks. two quick technical asks: 1) should we attempt to partially redact inside the prompt (e.g., mask email-like substrings) vs full prompt redact? 2) do we need an IAM approval ticket before toggling capture on?

jordan: prefer partial redact with strong regexes + token scrubbing. full prompt redact loses debugging signal. so: run prompt through two-pass scrubber: first regex mask for emails/ssns/cc numbers, then scrub bearer/api keys via header mask. also require an IAM approval ticket and a short github PR that references the incident ID.

leo: example regex I'll use for email mask: `s/([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+)@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+)\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/[REDACTED_EMAIL]/g` and for bearer tokens we add header-level drop. for user ids we'll do `sha256(user_id + env_salt)` and store that hash instead of raw.

maria: ok will implement. sample capture config I'm going to deploy (pseudo):
```
capture:
  enabled: false
  allowed_roles: [eng-ml, eng-security]
  store: s3://ephemeral-captures
  retention_seconds: 3600
  redact:
    prompt_regexes: [email, ssn, cc]
    header_blocklist: [Authorization, X-API-Key]
    token_scrub: true
```

ops-oncall: from ops perspective: we can flip a feature-flag that enables capture for a given incident id. need runbook for rollback and check that capture stream doesn't spiky CPU on inference nodes. can you test in canary before prod? also add CloudTrail/audit events for who toggled it.

maria: will test in canary then short prod window. I'll add audit events and a retention enforcement lambda to delete after 60m. will add PR and link the IAM ticket.

jordan: security sign-off conditions: 1) prompt masking regexes in place and unit-tested, 2) header blocklist enforced at proxy (not app), 3) salt & hash approach documented and salt stored in KMS, 4) time-limited bucket + access limited to named principals, 5) audit log entry required. if all met, approve a one-time 60min capture.

maria: thanks — I'll open the PR and the IAM ticket now. pinging here when ready for final thumbs up. :thumbsup:

leo: cheers — will review PR fast.

ops-oncall: will watch the rollout window and be on-call during the capture.

jordan: noted, will verify policy checklist after PR lands. :white_check_mark:
